IN NO EVENT SHALL ANY 18 - CONTRIBUTORS BE LIABLE FOR ANY DIRECT, INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, 19 - EXEMPLARY, OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES (INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, 20 - PROCUREMENT OF SUBSTITUTE GOODS OR SERVICES; LOSS OF USE, DATA, OR 21 - PROFITS; OR BUSINESS INTERRUPTION) HOWEVER CAUSED AND ON ANY THEORY 22 - OF LIABILITY, WHETHER IN CONTRACT, STRICT LIABILITY, OR TORT (INCLUDING 23 - NEGLIGENCE OR OTHERWISE) ARISING IN ANY WAY OUT OF THE USE OF THIS 24 - SOFTWARE, EVEN IF ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGE. 25 *====================================================================*/ 26 27 /*! 28 * \file bmpio.c 29 * 
    30   *
    31   *      Read bmp
    32   *           PIX          *pixReadStreamBmp()
    33   *           PIX          *pixReadMemBmp()
    34   *
    35   *      Write bmp
    36   *           l_int32       pixWriteStreamBmp()
    37   *           l_int32       pixWriteMemBmp()
    38   *
    39   *
40 */ 41 42 #ifdef HAVE_CONFIG_H 43 #include 44 #endif /* HAVE_CONFIG_H */ 45 46 #include 47 #include "allheaders.h" 48 #include "bmp.h" 49 50 /* --------------------------------------------*/ 51 #if USE_BMPIO /* defined in environ.h */ 52 /* --------------------------------------------*/ 53 54 /* Here we're setting the pixel value 0 to white (255) and the 55 * value 1 to black (0). This is the convention for grayscale, but 56 * the opposite of the convention for 1 bpp, where 0 is white 57 * and 1 is black. Both colormap entries are opaque (alpha = 255) */ 58 RGBA_QUAD bwmap[2] = { {255,255,255,255}, {0,0,0,255} }; 59 60 /* Colormap size limit */ 61 static const l_int32 L_MAX_ALLOWED_NUM_COLORS = 256; 62 63 /* Image dimension limits */ 64 static const l_int32 L_MAX_ALLOWED_WIDTH = 1000000; 65 static const l_int32 L_MAX_ALLOWED_HEIGHT = 1000000; 66 static const l_int64 L_MAX_ALLOWED_PIXELS = 400000000LL; 67 static const l_int32 L_MAX_ALLOWED_RES = 10000000; /* pixels/meter */ 68 69 #ifndef NO_CONSOLE_IO 70 #define DEBUG 0 71 #endif /* ~NO_CONSOLE_IO */ 72 73 /*--------------------------------------------------------------* 74 * Read bmp * 75 *--------------------------------------------------------------*/ 76 /*! 77 * \brief pixReadStreamBmp() 78 * 79 * \param[in] fp file stream opened for read 80 * \return pix, or NULL on error 81 * 82 * 
    83   * Notes:
    84   *      (1) Here are references on the bmp file format:
    85   *          http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMP_file_format
    86   *          http://www.fortunecity.com/skyscraper/windows/364/bmpffrmt.html
    87   *
88 */ 89 PIX * 90 pixReadStreamBmp(FILE *fp) 91 { 92 l_uint8 *data; 93 size_t size; 94 PIX *pix; 95 96 PROCNAME("pixReadStreamBmp"); 97 98 if (!fp) 99 return (PIX *)ERROR_PTR("fp not defined", procName, NULL); 100 101 /* Read data from file and decode into Y,U,V arrays */ 102 rewind(fp); 103 if ((data = l_binaryReadStream(fp, &size)) == NULL) 104 return (PIX *)ERROR_PTR("data not read", procName, NULL); 105 106 pix = pixReadMemBmp(data, size); 107 LEPT_FREE(data); 108 return pix; 109 } 110 111 112 /*! 113 * \brief pixReadMemBmp() 114 * 115 * \param[in] cdata bmp data 116 * \param[in] size number of bytes of bmp-formatted data 117 * \return pix, or NULL on error 118 * 119 * 
   120   * Notes:
   121   *      (1) The BMP file is organized as follows:
   122   *          * 14 byte fileheader
   123   *          * variable size infoheader, from 40 to 124 bytes.  We only use
   124   *            data in he first 40 bytes.
   125   *          * an optional colormap, with size 4 * ncolors (in bytes)
   126   *          * the image data
   127   *      (2) 2 bpp bmp files are not valid in the original spec, but they
   128   *          are valid in later versions.
   129   *
130 */ 131 PIX * 132 pixReadMemBmp(const l_uint8 *cdata, 133 size_t size) 134 { 135 l_uint8 pel[4]; 136 l_uint8 *cmapBuf, *fdata, *data; 137 l_int16 bftype, depth, d; 138 l_int32 offset, ihbytes, width, height, height_neg, xres, yres; 139 l_int32 compression, imagebytes, cmapbytes, cmapEntries; 140 l_int32 fdatabpl, extrabytes, pixWpl, pixBpl, i, j, k; 141 l_uint32 *line, *pixdata, *pword; 142 l_int64 npixels; 143 BMP_FH *bmpfh; 144 #if defined(__GNUC__) 145 BMP_HEADER *bmph; 146 #define bmpih (&bmph->bmpih) 147 #else 148 BMP_IH *bmpih; 149 #endif 150 PIX *pix, *pix1; 151 PIXCMAP *cmap; 152 153 PROCNAME("pixReadMemBmp"); 154 155 if (!cdata) 156 return (PIX *)ERROR_PTR("cdata not defined", procName, NULL); 157 if (size < sizeof(BMP_FH) + sizeof(BMP_IH)) 158 return (PIX *)ERROR_PTR("bmf size error", procName, NULL); 159 160 /* Verify this is an uncompressed bmp */ 161 bmpfh = (BMP_FH *)cdata; 162 bftype = bmpfh->bfType[0] + ((l_int32)bmpfh->bfType[1] << 8); 163 if (bftype != BMP_ID) 164 return (PIX *)ERROR_PTR("not bmf format", procName, NULL); 165 #if defined(__GNUC__) 166 bmph = (BMP_HEADER *)bmpfh; 167 #else 168 bmpih = (BMP_IH *)(cdata + BMP_FHBYTES); 169 #endif 170 compression = convertOnBigEnd32(bmpih->biCompression); 171 if (compression != 0) 172 return (PIX *)ERROR_PTR("cannot read compressed BMP files", 173 procName, NULL); 174 175 /* Find the offset from the beginning of the file to the image data */ 176 offset = bmpfh->bfOffBits[0]; 177 offset += (l_int32)bmpfh->bfOffBits[1] << 8; 178 offset += (l_int32)bmpfh->bfOffBits[2] << 16; 179 offset += (l_uint32)bmpfh->bfOffBits[3] << 24; 180 181 /* Read the remaining useful data in the infoheader. 182 * Note that the first 4 bytes give the infoheader size. */ 183 ihbytes = convertOnBigEnd32(*(l_uint32 *)(bmpih)); 184 width = convertOnBigEnd32(bmpih->biWidth); 185 height = convertOnBigEnd32(bmpih->biHeight); 186 depth = convertOnBigEnd16(bmpih->biBitCount); 187 imagebytes = convertOnBigEnd32(bmpih->biSizeImage); 188 xres = convertOnBigEnd32(bmpih->biXPelsPerMeter); 189 yres = convertOnBigEnd32(bmpih->biYPelsPerMeter); 190 191 /* Some sanity checking. We impose limits on the image 192 * dimensions, resolution and number of pixels. We make sure the 193 * file is the correct size to hold the amount of uncompressed data 194 * that is specified in the header. The number of colormap 195 * entries is checked: it can be either 0 (no cmap) or some 196 * number between 2 and 256. 197 * Note that the imagebytes for uncompressed images is either 198 * 0 or the size of the file data. (The fact that it can 199 * be 0 is perhaps some legacy glitch). */ 200 if (width < 1) 201 return (PIX *)ERROR_PTR("width < 1", procName, NULL); 202 if (width > L_MAX_ALLOWED_WIDTH) 203 return (PIX *)ERROR_PTR("width too large", procName, NULL); 204 if (height == 0 || height < -L_MAX_ALLOWED_HEIGHT || 205 height > L_MAX_ALLOWED_HEIGHT) 206 return (PIX *)ERROR_PTR("invalid height", procName, NULL); 207 if (xres < 0 || xres > L_MAX_ALLOWED_RES || 208 yres < 0 || yres > L_MAX_ALLOWED_RES) 209 return (PIX *)ERROR_PTR("invalid resolution", procName, NULL); 210 height_neg = 0; 211 if (height < 0) { 212 height_neg = 1; 213 height = -height; 214 } 215 npixels = 1LL * width * height; 216 if (npixels > L_MAX_ALLOWED_PIXELS) 217 return (PIX *)ERROR_PTR("npixels too large", procName, NULL); 218 if (depth != 1 && depth != 2 && depth != 4 && depth != 8 && 219 depth != 16 && depth != 24 && depth != 32) 220 return (PIX *)ERROR_PTR("depth not in {1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 24, 32}", --- 1 * \brief pixReadMem() 2 * 3 * \param[in] data const; encoded 4 * \param[in] size size of data 5 * \return pix, or NULL on error 6 * 7 * 
     8   * Notes:
     9   *      (1) This is a variation of pixReadStream(), where the data is read
    10   *          from a memory buffer rather than a file.
    11   *      (2) On windows, this only reads tiff formatted files directly from
    12   *          memory.  For other formats, it writes to a temp file and
    13   *          decompresses from file.
    14   *      (3) findFileFormatBuffer() requires up to 12 bytes to decide on
    15   *          the format.  That determines the constraint here.  But in
    16   *          fact the data must contain the entire compressed string for
    17   *          the image.
    18   *
19 */ 20 PIX * 21 pixReadMem(const l_uint8 *data, 22 size_t size) 23 { 24 l_int32 format, valid; 25 PIX *pix; 26 PIXCMAP *cmap; 27 28 PROCNAME("pixReadMem"); 29 30 if (!data) 31 return (PIX *)ERROR_PTR("data not defined", procName, NULL); 32 if (size < 12) 33 return (PIX *)ERROR_PTR("size < 12", procName, NULL); 34 pix = NULL; 35 36 findFileFormatBuffer(data, &format); 37 switch (format) 38 { 39 case IFF_BMP: 40 if ((pix = pixReadMemBmp(data, size)) == NULL ) 41 return (PIX *)ERROR_PTR( "bmp: no pix returned", procName, NULL); 42 break; 43 44 case IFF_JFIF_JPEG: 45 if ((pix = pixReadMemJpeg(data, size, 0, 1, NULL, 0)) == NULL) 46 return (PIX *)ERROR_PTR( "jpeg: no pix returned", procName, NULL); 47 break; 48 49 case IFF_PNG: 50 if ((pix = pixReadMemPng(data, size)) == NULL) 51 return (PIX *)ERROR_PTR("png: no pix returned", procName, NULL); 52 break; 53 54 case IFF_TIFF: 55 case IFF_TIFF_PACKBITS: 56 case IFF_TIFF_RLE: 57 case IFF_TIFF_G3: 58 case IFF_TIFF_G4: 59 case IFF_TIFF_LZW: 60 case IFF_TIFF_ZIP: 61 /* Reading page 0 by default */ 62 if ((pix = pixReadMemTiff(data, size, 0)) == NULL) 63 return (PIX *)ERROR_PTR("tiff: no pix returned", procName, NULL); 64 break; 65 66 case IFF_PNM: 67 if ((pix = pixReadMemPnm(data, size)) == NULL) 68 return (PIX *)ERROR_PTR("pnm: no pix returned", procName, NULL); 69 break; 70 71 case IFF_GIF: 72 if ((pix = pixReadMemGif(data, size)) == NULL) 73 return (PIX *)ERROR_PTR("gif: no pix returned", procName, NULL); 74 break; 75 76 case IFF_JP2: 77 if ((pix = pixReadMemJp2k(data, size, 1, NULL, 0, 0)) == NULL) 78 return (PIX *)ERROR_PTR("jp2k: no pix returned", procName, NULL); 79 break; 80 81 case IFF_WEBP: --- 1 pixRotateShear(PIX *pixs, 2 l_int32 xcen, 3 l_int32 ycen, 4 l_float32 angle, 5 l_int32 incolor) 6 { 7 PROCNAME("pixRotateShear"); 8 9 if (!pixs) 10 return (PIX *)(PIX *)ERROR_PTR("pixs not defined", procName, NULL); 11 if (incolor != L_BRING_IN_WHITE && incolor != L_BRING_IN_BLACK) 12 return (PIX *)(PIX *)ERROR_PTR("invalid incolor value", procName, NULL); 13 14 if (L_ABS(angle) > MaxShearAngle) { 15 L_ERROR("%6.2f radians; too large for shear rotation\n", procName, 16 L_ABS(angle)); 17 return NULL; 18 } 19 if (L_ABS(angle) < MinAngleToRotate) 20 return pixClone(pixs); 21 22 if (L_ABS(angle) <= MaxTwoShearAngle) 23 return pixRotate2Shear(pixs, xcen, ycen, angle, incolor); 24 else 25 return pixRotate3Shear(pixs, xcen, ycen, angle, incolor); 26 } 27 28 29 /*! 30 * \brief pixRotate2Shear() 31 * 32 * \param[in] pixs any depth; cmap ok 33 * \param[in] xcen, ycen center of rotation 34 * \param[in] angle radians 35 * \param[in] incolor L_BRING_IN_WHITE, L_BRING_IN_BLACK; 36 * \return pixd, or NULL on error. 37 * 38 * 
    39   * Notes:
    40   *      (1) This rotates the image about the given point, using the 2-shear
    41   *          method.  It should only be used for angles no larger than
    42   *          MaxTwoShearAngle.  For larger angles, a warning is issued.
    43   *      (2) A positive angle gives a clockwise rotation.
    44   *      (3) 2-shear rotation by a specified angle is equivalent
    45   *          to the sequential transformations
    46   *             x' = x + tan(angle) * (y - ycen)     for x-shear
    47   *             y' = y + tan(angle) * (x - xcen)     for y-shear
    48   *      (4) Computation of tan(angle) is performed within the shear operation.
    49   *      (5) This brings in 'incolor' pixels from outside the image.
    50   *      (6) If the image has an alpha layer, it is rotated separately by
    51   *          two shears.
    52   *
53 */
